text:
Mia Chen: FYI escalation from ACME on their private deployment. They see SSE streams frequently drop right before the final \u2018done\u2019 marker, client reconnects and sometimes gets duplicate outputs. Customer says this only happens when requests route through their Windows-based corporate proxy/ingress (IIS+ARR) in front of our on-prem gateway.

Samir Patel: Can you paste the minimal repro? headers, curl, and whether they're using HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2?

Mia Chen: Repro from customer (sanitized):

```
# reproducer they gave
TOKEN=REDACTED
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --no-buffer "https://private.acme.internal/api/v1/stream?model=xlarge"
```

They say it works fine when they hit the gateway directly, but when the request goes through corp-proxy -> onprem-ingress -> our gateway it frequently ends with a half event and client sees connection close. No 5xx from our side.

Javier Alvarez: Do they have any MTU/Jumbo frame config in their VPC? Fragmentation on TLS can sometimes split SSE chunk boundaries in odd ways when proxies reassemble.

Mia Chen: Yes, they reported their VPC uses jumbo frames (MTU 9000) while their edge proxy is on a corporate network that enforces 1500. They mentioned some network team changes recently.

Kara Li: Interesting. Two likely axes: (1) proxy/ingress buffering semantics (IIS/ARR often buffers full response or alters chunk framing), (2) MTU/TCP segmentation causing TLS record fragmentation and downstream proxies treating partial TLS records as keepalive failures. Both can cause truncated SSE events or delayed flushes.

Samir Patel: Requesting packet capture and proxy config. Ask them to run a short tcpdump on the proxy/gateway showing the TLS record boundaries and also capture the raw SSE bytes at our gateway (we have a tracing flag).

Mia Chen: They attached a pcap excerpt. Key findings: repeated TLS records of ~1200 bytes, then a small 200B final record that contains the tail of the last SSE chunk. The IIS ARR proxy has a setting `responseBufferLimit` and `enableKernelBuffer` turned ON.

Javier Alvarez: That aligns with buffering: ARR is likely aggregating and rewriting chunk sizes or holding small writes until a threshold. For SSE we need the streaming flush semantics (small SSE lines) to be sent as-is. If ARR buffers until X bytes are available, clients will see delayed or partial events. Also some proxies transform `Transfer-Encoding` which breaks streaming semantics.

Mia Chen: Customer logs show their client got a TCP FIN shortly after receiving the partial data. Client reconnects using no Last-Event-ID (their client doesn't set it). That explains duplication on reconnect. They also reported a spike in billed tokens because their app retried and resumed new sessions.

Samir Patel: Actionable repro we asked them to try immediately: (1) bypass ARR (direct to gateway) to confirm, (2) on ARR set `preserveHostHeader` and disable response buffering, (3) try forcing HTTP/1.1 on the client: `-H "Connection: keep-alive" --http1.1 --no-buffer` and (4) run tcpdump with `tcpdump -i eth0 -s0 -w /tmp/stream.pcap host <gateway> and port 443`.

Kara Li: Also ask them to test reducing MTU on the VPC interface (or enable MSS clamping) to avoid TLS fragmentation crossing the corp-proxy boundary. Temporary workaround: our side can emit periodic SSE comments to keep small writes bigger, e.g. send `:hb\n\n` every 10s, or batch the final payload to avoid tiny final TLS records. Not ideal but a stopgap.

Mia Chen: Customer tried disabling ARR buffering and the issue frequency dropped to ~1/20 streams. After setting MSS clamp on their border router to 1440 the failure rate went to zero in 2 hours.

Javier Alvarez: Good. We should capture follow-ups: (A) eng-runtime - verify our TLS write flush behavior on Windows vs Linux and ensure we coalesce writes so tiny final record doesn't end up alone, (B) eng-ml / client SDK - add guidance to retries to use Last-Event-ID or a lightweight resume token to dedupe on reconnect, (C) eng-sre - consider recommending MSS clamping doc in Private deployment checklist and an ARR-specific config note.

Samir Patel: I'll open tasks:
- ENG-RUNTIME-# (owner Javier) - investigate coalescing small writes and add opt-in heartbeat chunking
- ENG-CLIENT-# (owner Kara) - add Last-Event-ID guidance + example reconnection backoff
- SRE-PRIVATE-# (owner Samir) - private deploy runbook update for MTU / proxy settings

Kara Li: For immediate customer mitigation we recommended: 1) set ARR `responseBuffering="disabled"` and disable kernel buffering, 2) set their edge router to clamp MSS to 1400-1440, 3) temporarily enable a 10s SSE heartbeat from the app. They implemented 1+2 and confirmed stable.

Mia Chen: Customer is happy with the workaround; asked if we can add a note in Private onboarding about Windows ARR and corporate proxies.

Javier Alvarez: Agreed. Also logging: we should detect partial final events on our side (timeout after last data chunk without \u2018event: done\u2019) and emit an internal telemetry bump to signal proxy-related truncation. I can prototype a detector.

Samir Patel: Thanks team. Mia, please send the pcap + ARR config to eng-runtime and SRE, add links here. Once we have the prototype detector we'll roll a canary to Dedicated staging.

oncall-bot: NOTE: escalation created: INC-2026-1183, assigned to eng-runtime (Javier Alvarez) and eng-sre (Samir Patel).

Mia Chen: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: closing the loop with ACME now and will paste final confirmation once they validate in 24h.
